items.name: AFL++
items.source_story_title: Java4Shell: RCE in OpenJDK when processing Base64
items.summary: Fuzzing toolkit credited with finding kernel bugs while an LLM handled glue code.
items.why_included: A concrete first-hand account of useful AI-assisted security work.
items.evidence: eru reports discovering Linux kernel problems and credits AFL++ with the substantive fuzzing work, while Kimi wrote glue code.

evidence_sources.author: eru
evidence_sources.excerpt: I used Kimi to drive the fuzzer. The model didn't have to do anything smart, just do the tedious work of writing the glue code to make the fuzzing work. AFL++ did the 'smart' parts, and I had the idea to kick it off and oversaw the patches.

items.name: kdb+
items.source_story_title: Rows vs. Columns: How different are they, really?
items.summary: Columnar time-series database praised for its simple implementation and understandable memory layout.
items.why_included: A named alternative with specific architectural praise, not a neutral database mention.
items.evidence: ronfriedhaber calls kdb+ their preferred columnar implementation and praises its simplicity and transparent data layout.

evidence_sources.author: ronfriedhaber
evidence_sources.excerpt: KDB+ is the best implementation of a columnar DB in my opinion. Simple C, and one can understand how the data is stored down to the DRAM cells.
